analysis.title: OpenAI vs Anthropic: two paths to profit
key_insights: OpenAI is building a consumer platform funded increasingly by advertising, with its own apps, browser and a planned device. Anthropic sells intelligence by the token to companies and developers, mostly through cloud marketplaces, and has pledged to stay ad-free.
Anthropic filed its S-1 with the SEC on 26 October. OpenAI filed confidentially in June and has said it will not list this year.
OpenAI enterprise revenue overtook consumer revenue per the CFO in August, and the enterprise run rate grew 107% in Q3. ChatGPT reached one billion weekly users this summer.
Anthropic's S-1 shows 80% of H1 2026 revenue was consumption-based (mostly API) and 20% subscriptions. 48% of revenue came through AWS, Google Cloud and Azure marketplaces.
More than 11,900 Anthropic customers each generated over $100,000 of revenue in the twelve months to September, up from about 950 a year earlier.
OpenAI ads went live 9 February at a reported $60 CPM on the Free and Go tiers in the US. ChatGPT's ad business passed a $1bn annualised run rate in early October.
Per Axios, OpenAI has told investors it expects about $2.5bn of ad revenue this year, $11bn in 2027, $25bn in 2028 and $100bn by 2030.

OpenAI's 2025 operating loss was about $21bn per leaked documents, and it carries hundreds of billions of dollars of multi-year compute commitments. Investors back it at a private valuation of around $1.4tn.
OpenAI execution has been uneven: it shut down the Sora app in March and lost a planned $1bn Disney investment, and it discontinued Instant Checkout after weak uptake.

Alphabet is the most exposed incumbent if OpenAI's ad plan works. Google Search runs at more than $250bn a year against roughly $1bn for ChatGPT ads. Search growth slowed to 12% in Q3 from 17% and 19%, and Alphabet shares fell about 8% after results on 28 October even as Google Cloud revenue roughly doubled.

Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson argues ChatGPT ad budgets will come mainly out of Search and that consumer attention is zero-sum, which also exposes YouTube. The report's own view is that the more realistic risk is gradual erosion of Search pricing power.

Anthropic revenue rose from $41mn in 2023 to $4.6bn in 2025 and $16.3bn in H1 2026, about 14 times the prior-year period. Q2 revenue was $11.6bn with $974mn GAAP operating income. Q3 revenue rose 47% to nearly $17bn with $2.5bn adjusted operating income and a $567mn GAAP operating loss.

Anthropic weaknesses: about 20% of H1 revenue came from two customers, almost half flows through cloud partners that compete with their own models, it has committed at least $518bn to cloud and compute over the next decade, and OpenAI has reportedly won some customers with discounts.

Run-rate figures are not comparable. Anthropic counts the gross value of some sales through cloud partners and OpenAI counts only its share. OpenAI cited about $50bn at end-September, not the $70bn reported in early October, and targets $70bn by year-end. Anthropic was above $65bn at end-July.

The report concludes the two deserve different valuation frameworks. OpenAI is the Google of AI, and Anthropic is closer to Microsoft plus an infrastructure provider. OpenAI's variables are engagement, ad yield per user and trust. Anthropic's are enterprise retention, inference gross margins, customer concentration and compute discipline.

market_movers.rationale: ChatGPT ads are a close substitute for Search ads and could erode Search pricing power. Scale keeps the threat in proportion, and Alphabet has Gemini, AI Mode and ads in AI answers as defences.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 results reported 28 October: Search growth slowed to 12% from 17% and 19% in the previous two quarters, shares fell about 8% after the print, and Google Cloud revenue roughly doubled.

Anthropic (S-1 and Q3 figures as cited): Q2 2026 revenue $11.6bn with $974mn GAAP operating income. Q3 revenue rose 47% to nearly $17bn with $2.5bn adjusted operating income and a $567mn GAAP operating loss.
risk_factors: OpenAI: advertising could change the product and erode user trust, with regulatory and legal scrutiny such as a Texas lawsuit over child safety.
OpenAI: large operating losses and hundreds of billions of dollars in multi-year compute commitments.
Anthropic: customer concentration, with about 20% of H1 revenue from two customers.
Anthropic: almost half of revenue flows through cloud partners that are also competitors.
Anthropic: at least $518bn of compute and cloud commitments over the next decade, a fixed obligation if demand cools.
Price competition is intensifying, with OpenAI reportedly winning some Anthropic customers through discounts.
Run-rate figures for the two companies are not directly comparable, so which is larger is unresolved until audited figures arrive.

tension_points.bull_case: ChatGPT ads are the closest substitute for a Google search ad, and Gil Luria expects ad budgets to come mainly out of Search. OpenAI targets $100bn of ad revenue by 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Search runs at more than $250bn a year against roughly $1bn for ChatGPT ads, and OpenAI's 2030 target is still below what Search earns today. Alphabet's Gemini app and AI Mode each reach about a billion monthly users and it is rolling out ads in AI answers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Search growth slowing further from 12% in Q3 would support the threat. The report names no specific breaking level.

tension_points.bull_case: Customers pay per token so spending scales with value created. Revenue was $16.3bn in H1 2026, Q2 had GAAP operating income, and 11,900 customers each exceed $100,000.
tension_points.bear_case: About 20% of H1 revenue came from two customers, almost half flows through competing cloud partners, and at least $518bn of compute is committed over the next decade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand cooling against the fixed compute obligation, or enterprise retention and gross margins on inference weakening.

theme_stances.key_argument: Advertising is the proven way to monetise the long tail of free users at internet scale, so the pivot is arguably inevitable.
Its path to profitability is clearer than OpenAI's, though upside depends on AI becoming integral to enterprise infrastructure.
theme_stances.evidence: Its path to profitability is clearer

theme_stances.key_argument: The more realistic risk for Search is a gradual erosion of pricing power rather than a sudden loss.
